title: The reach of a corner lot (the real lot and three made-up rectangles)
summary: How far a corner lot reaches from each street line and from the corner point, which decides whether the 100-percent corner coverage and the rear-yard waiver cover the whole lot. It covers the real lot (215-16 Northern Boulevard) and three made-up rectangles C1, C2 and C3. Every value comes from measurements of the recorded outline (or the chosen rectangle sizes) and the law text, never from a program run.
what_it_is_worth: Prepared by an AI helper and recomputed by a second AI; their agreement alone is not proof. The real lot's reaches are measured from the approximate tax-map outline; C1, C2 and C3 are made-up rectangles chosen to show the corner-lot-portion and rear-yard thresholds. It is a draft reading, not professionally reviewed. The corner-lot-portion definition it uses (ZR 12-10) is not captured.
what_it_does_not_establish: The real lot's reaches are measured from an approximate outline, not a survey; the strip and wedge areas are grid approximations.
C1, C2 and C3 are made-up rectangles, not real properties.
It relies on the ZR 12-10 corner-lot-portion definition, which is not captured.
It is not a professional or legal determination.
prepared_by: An AI helper that took no part in writing the program's rules, working only from a sealed folder of pinned law-text captures and the lot's recorded facts, with no access to the program.
checked_by: A second AI recomputed the arithmetic and the geometry independently from the same sealed folder. Agreement between two AI answers alone is not proof.
sources: The independent hand-calculation, follow-up (tables C and D): provenance/return-independent-hand-calculation-2.md
The sealed folder given to the helper: the pinned ZR captures (without the notes describing how the program encoded them) and the lot's recorded official facts, with no program access.
The law captures under docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/, each pinned by its content digest.

rows.why_applies: These reaches decide whether the whole lot is the corner-lot portion (within 100 feet of each street line) and whether the rear-yard waiver (within 100 feet of the corner point) covers the whole lot.

expected.value: from the Northern Boulevard street line the lot reaches at most 99.97 ft; from the 215 Place street line at most 103.93 ft; from the corner point at most 144.60 ft. The whole lot is within 100 ft of the Northern Boulevard street line but not of the 215 Place street line (a strip about 3.93 ft wide, about 390 sq ft, lies beyond), and not within 100 ft of the corner point (about 2,560 sq ft lies beyond)

rows.does_not_establish: These are measurements from the approximate tax-map outline (the strip and wedge areas are grid approximations), not a survey; by themselves they give no coverage percentage or rear-yard requirement.

citations.title: Maximum lot coverage in R6 through R12 Districts
citations.quote: the maximum residential lot coverage for interior lots or through lots shall be 80 percent and the maximum residential lot coverage for corner lots shall be 100 percent

citations.title: Definitions
citations.quote: that portion bounded by the intersecting street line and lines parallel to and 100 feet from each intersecting street line
citations.status_note: The repository capture of ZR 12-10 holds only the wide-street and narrow-street definitions; the lot-type and corner-lot-portion definitions are not captured and wait for step P1.

rows.why_applies: The 100-percent corner-lot rule (ZR 23-362(a)) covers only the ZR 12-10 corner-lot portion, within 100 feet of each street line; part of this lot lies beyond 100 feet of the 215 Place street line.

expected.reason: The lot reaches 103.93 feet from the 215 Place street line, so it is not wholly within the corner-lot portion and there is no single whole-lot coverage figure. The ZR 12-10 corner-lot-portion definition is not captured.

rows.source_reference: return-independent-hand-calculation-2.md, Q1(a)-(b), and the work order's table C ('not known').

citations.title: Additional rear yard modifications
citations.quote: no rear yard shall be required within 100 feet of the point of intersection of two street lines intersecting at an angle of 135 degrees or less

citations.title: Additional rear yard modifications
citations.quote: In R6 through R12 Districts, no rear yard shall be required where such rear lot line coincides with a side lot line of an adjoining zoning lot

rows.why_applies: Within 100 feet of the corner no rear yard is required (ZR 23-344(a)); beyond 100 feet of the street line the side-lot-line portion is treated as a rear lot line (ZR 23-344(c)), and whether a rear yard is then required depends on whether that line coincides with a neighbour's lot line and on ZR 23-342 (depth), which are not available.

expected.reason: Along the 50-foot strip beyond 100 feet of the street line, whether a rear yard is required depends on the neighbouring lot lines (ZR 23-344(c)(1) and (c)(3)) and on ZR 23-342 (depth), which are not available, so it is not known. Within 100 feet of the corner, ZR 23-344(a) waives it.

rows.does_not_establish: It does not settle the rear yard along the strip beyond the corner-lot portion.
